full_judgment: 2. Facts, in short, are that petitioner, Privatisation Board, hereinafter in brief the Board, invited International Tender on 27th May, 1997 to sell Kohinoor Battery Manufacturers Ltd at 143- 145, Tejgaon Industrial Area. The respondent No.1 submitted tender for purchasing the same quoting Taka 16,00,9990 and accordingly paid the earnest money of Taka 40,00,250 and he became highest bidder, that Board issued letter of intent datd11February, 99 in favour of the respondent No.1 to sell the enterprise at the amount offered by him plus more or less, the amount 1,95,85,000 being the enterprise's long term loan and also with certain other conditions, that respondent No.1 accuepted the letter of intent and paid the remaining amount first to be paid being 25% of the bid money i.e. the amount of Taka 3,60,02,249.75 in addition to the earnest money within the stipulated period of 30 days from the date of letter of intent. Respondent No.1 filed an application on 20th June, 1999 addressed to the Chairman of the Disinvestment Board stating that he had been making arrangement to pay the balance in cash and he needed a letter confirming that 15% rebate would be allowed in that case but the Board gave no reply that Agrani Bank had filed a suit for recovery of Taka 23 crore, against the enterprise, that there upon respondent No.1 sent the letter on 22nd June, 1999 to the Board intimating that if no arrangement is made with the Agrani Bank it would be impossible for him to take over the factory by 1st July, 1999, the Board did not reply to the said letter. Respondent No.1 wrote several letters to the Board for handing over factory to him and he also wrote letter to the Ministry of Finance and to the Additional Secretary, Ministry of Finance seeking their intervention in the matter but in vain. Thereafter the respondent No.1 upon serving notice demanding justice upon the Board on 28th February, 2000 moved the High Court Division in writ jurisdiction and obtained the Rule on 29th February, 2000.
